properties.name: management.endpoint.security-auth.access
properties.description: Permitted level of access for the securityAuth endpoint.

properties.name: management.endpoint.security-auth.cache.time-to-live
properties.description: Maximum time that a response can be cached.

properties.name: security.auth.audience
properties.description: Expected audience (`aud` claim). Left blank to skip audience validation.

properties.name: security.auth.clock-skew-seconds
properties.description: Allowed clock skew, in seconds, when checking expiry/not-before.

properties.name: security.auth.header-name
properties.description: HTTP header the token is read from.

properties.name: security.auth.header-prefix
properties.description: Prefix stripped from the header value before parsing, e.g. "Bearer ".

properties.name: security.auth.hmac-secret
properties.description: HMAC shared secret (base64), for HS256/384/512. Set this OR publicKey/jwks-uri, not both - HMAC is the simple zero-infra default for a single-issuer internal platform; prefer an asymmetric key or a JWKS endpoint when tokens are issued by a separate identity provider, since HMAC requires sharing the same secret with whatever issues tokens.

properties.name: security.auth.issuer
properties.description: Expected issuer (`iss` claim). Tokens from any other issuer are rejected.

properties.name: security.auth.reject-invalid-token
properties.description: If a token is present but fails validation, respond 401 immediately (true) rather than letting the request proceed unauthenticated (false). A MISSING token always proceeds unauthenticated either way - this only governs the "token present but invalid" case, so public endpoints on the same service are unaffected.

properties.name: security.auth.roles-claim
properties.description: Claim name holding the caller's roles - expected to be a list/array of strings.

properties.name: management.endpoint.security-auth.enabled
properties.description: Whether to enable the securityAuth endpoint.
